report:
A, B, and C agreed to the shared NCE list and the final plan. C has no corrections or disagreements.

The plan is to stop using the leaking espresso machine, unplug it if safe, or mark it "do not use" if unplugging is unsafe. The grinder stays separate and remains in use unless someone identifies a problem with it. No one will move, discard, repair, or buy anything yet. B will send one short note to the office manager asking about formal ownership, repair history, office rules, and who can approve repairs or purchases. The note will also ask whether the office manager will authorize one qualified repair assessment and any fee.

No paid check will be booked before approval. If the office manager approves, one qualified person will give a written estimate, a safety view, and likely reliability. A, B, and C will then use one short written check-in in a short slot B can manage. Repair will go ahead only if it is safe, reliable, low upkeep, approved, and within the office manager's limits. If not, the office manager will advise on what to do with the machine, with B included in that step, and a simpler replacement will be considered only after approval. If ownership or approval stays unclear, the machine remains unused where it is.

No one takes on an ongoing repair job or cleaning rota, and C will not chase or handle the repair. I did not decide ownership or approve spending.
